summary: Server singleton of esv::RewardManager: two per-entity maps used while filling reward inventories - lists of entities and lists of item transfer requests. Cleared and refilled by RewardManager::ProcessGiveRewardRequests; read by RewardManager::ProcessRewardGivenRequests and esv::inventory::InteractionRequestSystem. Seen.py context: singleton present in the idle level, all zero.

fields.name: Item
fields.evidence: esv::reward::TransferRewardsRequest +0 (see esv.reward.TransferRewardsRequestComponent.json): ID from the ForEachEntityInInventory callback.

fields.name: Amount
fields.evidence: unsigned short of the same callback.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0xD59250 ProcessGiveRewardRequests gets the singleton (EoCServer.dll+0xD53AD0, stride 0x80, error path names FillRewardInventoriesRequestComponent) and calls EoCServer.dll+0x3BD4B0 on +0 - destroys values asserting IndexedStorage<DynamicArray<ls::ID<ecs::EntityHandleTraits>>> (hash-table tag) - then clears it. Key type assumed EntityHandle (not seen directly).

fields.name: TransferRequests
fields.evidence: Same function calls EoCServer.dll+0xD57200 on +0x40: destroys values asserting IndexedStorage<DynamicArray<esv::reward::TransferRewardsRequest>>; macOS has only HashMap<ls::ID<EntityHandleTraits>, DynamicArray<TransferRewardsRequest>>. bg3.exe+0x30EFB40 allocates 0x80 and zeroes two HashMap shapes.

open_questions: Meaning of the entity lists at +0 and which entities key both maps.
